title: Residency Artifact Collector and Attestation Automation for Dedicated Tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers on Dedicated require an auditable, tamper-evident proof bundle that demonstrates tenant residency (region of compute), network isolation boundaries, and retention policy enforcement. Current evidence is ad-hoc: manual screenshots, ad-hoc log extracts, and varying artifact formats. This makes renewals and third-party audits slow and error-prone.

Objective: Implement an automated pipeline that collects residency and isolation artifacts from Dedicated stacks, normalizes them into a standardized proof bundle, signs the bundle, stores deterministic copies in a custody location, and emits an attestation report suitable for customer download or inclusion in compliance packages. The system must integrate with tenant metadata, deployment inventory, audit logs, and retention enforcement systems.

Scope: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) across AWS and GCP regions initially. Includes: automated artifact collection, bundle schema definition, signature service integration, retention-proof snapshots (timestamped), evidence export API for customers and compliance teams, and a scheduled attestation generator for periodic deliveries. Not in scope: on-prem air-gapped installs (will follow in separate ticket).

Why now: Sales/legal requests increasing; manual evidence generation creates scaling risk for renewals; SOC/ISO auditors expect machine-readable attestations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Collector runs against a Dedicated tenant and returns a normalized artifact bundle containing: region tags, instance metadata, VPC/route table snapshot, active security group rules, storage bucket location and encryption metadata, recent audit-log segment, and retention policy snapshot.
A2: Bundle is immutably stored in the evidence store and cryptographically signed; signature can be verified with a Redwood public key.
A3: Attestation report generator creates a human-readable PDF and machine-readable JSON report linked to the bundle with timestamps and schema version.
A4: Export API allows customers with appropriate RBAC to request proof bundles for their tenant; request returns a one-time-download URL and audit entry.
A5: CI + e2e tests cover collector run for both AWS and GCP sample tenants and validate schema and signatures.
design_notes: Collector agent will run as a short-lived Kubernetes job within the Dedicated control plane with read-only IAM role scoped to the tenant's resources. It will query cloud metadata, VPC configs, and the platform's audit-log exporter.

"Bundle schema v1" will be JSON-LD based to make provenance explicit; fields: tenant_id, tenant_name, region, resource_inventory, retention_policy_snapshot, audit_log_segment (sha256), manifest, signature. Include schema version and collector build_id.

Use existing evidence-store S3/GCS buckets with object lock enabled for WORM retention; store both signed bundle and PDF report. Leverage KMS for envelope encryption and integrate with HSM-backed signing for production attestations.

Attestation generator will populate standard sections: executive summary, technical facts, chain-of-custody, and automated checks results. Align wording with legal/compliance team templates (Confluence doc linked in artifacts).
Authentication: use tenant-scoped service principal; API requests validated by console-roles. Export API must log requestor identity and emit audit events to the platform audit stream.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement collector and local evidence storage; run nightly for 5 pilot tenants in us-west-2 and europe-west1.
Phase 2: Add signing integration and export API; expose to pilot customers under NDA for feedback; collect legal signoff on PDF wording.
Phase 3: Expand to all Dedicated regions; enable scheduled monthly attestations and on-demand export; add UI link in Console under Tenant > Compliance > Evidence.
Fallback: If collector fails for a tenant, produce a clear failure artifact and create a ticket with collected partial evidence for manual review.
test_plan: Unit tests for bundle schema validation and manifest generation.
Integration tests: deploy collector in staging Dedicated cluster; run against seeded fake tenant resources for AWS/GCP and assert fields exist and signatures verify.
E2E smoke: Trigger export API and download bundle; verify PDF contains expected region and retention statements and that the bundle verifies with public key.
Load test: Simulate 200 concurrent on-demand export requests to validate rate limiting and queueing behavior.
monitoring_and_alerts: Metric: collector_job_success_rate per tenant; alert if < 99.5% over 24h.
Metric: evidence_store_write_latency and write_failures; page on > 5 failures in 10 minutes.
Audit: every export API call must generate an audit event with fields: tenant_id, requestor, ip, bundle_id, result.
Security: sign operation failures should trigger high-sev alert; require manual escalation to security on production HSM errors.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Collector needs broad read permissions and could be abused. Mitigation: enforce least-privilege role, short-lived credentials, and strict logging; run in control plane only with hardened network policies.
Risk: Signed bundles could be forged if key compromised. Mitigation: HSM-backed signing and key rotation policy; publish revocation list and support bundle re-issuance.
Risk: Large audit-log segments increase bundle size. Mitigation: include log segment hash and pointer to retention-restricted log storage rather than full logs for large windows.
